original_question: (Well-known question). A discrete group G is said to have the Haagerup property(also known as Gromov’s a-T-menability property) if there exists a metrically proper isometric action of G on a(possibly infinite-dimensional) Hilbert space. Are all 1-relator groups Haagerup groups?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.30 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)", asking whether every 1-relator group has the Haagerup property, with the Haagerup property defined there via a metrically proper isometric action on a possibly infinite-dimensional Hilbert space.
correct_elements: The draft already captures the paper’s intended problem almost exactly: it asks whether all 1-relator groups have the Haagerup property, and it includes the same defining criterion for the Haagerup property and the same synonym, Gromov’s a-T-menability.
missing_details: The paper states the question for discrete groups, so that ambient hypothesis should be kept explicitly.
To make the question fully stand-alone, "1-relator group" should be unpacked as a group admitting a one-relator presentation.
The paper places no additional restrictions on the one-relator groups under consideration, so the refined wording should make clear that the quantifier ranges over all such groups.

For maximal precision, it is cleaner to ask whether every 1-relator group "has the Haagerup property" rather than using the informal noun phrase "Haagerup group", even though the paper itself uses that phrasing.
refined_question: Does every discrete group admitting a one-relator presentation have the Haagerup property, meaning that it admits a metrically proper isometric action on some possibly infinite-dimensional Hilbert space?
justification: Problem 21.30 is the nearest official formulation in the paper and matches the draft almost verbatim. In the paper, the question is presented as a standalone open problem together with the definition of the Haagerup property, and no narrower hypothesis or explicitly proved equivalent reformulation is supplied there. The only sharpening needed is to preserve the paper’s explicit ambient hypothesis "discrete group" and to make "1-relator group" self-contained.
